learning_plan.focus: Deep Learning Fundamentals & Advanced PyTorch/TensorFlow Proficiency

daily_breakdown.1_hour: ML/DL Theory Refresh: Linear Algebra, Calculus (relevant parts for ML), Probability & Statistics (Bayes' Theorem, hypothesis testing), Supervised/Unsupervised Learning (review), Neural Networks (activation functions, backpropagation, optimizers, regularization), CNNs, RNNs/Transformers basics.
daily_breakdown.1.5_hours: Project 1: Implement an advanced image classification model. For instance, fine-tune a pre-trained ResNet or EfficientNet on a slightly more complex dataset like CIFAR-100, or a small Kaggle image dataset. Focus on robust experimentation and clean, modular code.

key_topics: Deep Neural Network Architectures (ResNet, VGG, etc.), Optimization, Regularization
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Transfer Learning techniques
Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) / Transformers (conceptual understanding for application)
PyTorch/TensorFlow API mastery (nn.Module, DataLoader, optimizers, callbacks, TensorBoard)
resources: fast.ai Practical Deep Learning for Coders (for PyTorch)
Deep Learning Specialization (Coursera, Andrew Ng) - For foundational DL
Kaggle notebooks for advanced implementation examples

daily_breakdown.1_hour: MLOps Concepts: CI/CD for ML pipelines, data versioning (DVC concepts), model monitoring basics, experiment tracking (MLflow concepts and basic usage).
daily_breakdown.1.5_hours: Project 2: Take Project 1 (the image classifier), containerize it with Docker. Build a FastAPI endpoint to serve predictions from the trained model. Deploy this API to a free-tier cloud service (e.g., Heroku, Render, or a basic AWS EC2/GCP Cloud Run instance for hands-on experience).

key_topics: Git & GitHub (advanced workflows: branching, merging, pull requests)
FastAPI/Flask (web server for ML model deployment)
Basic Cloud Computing (AWS Sagemaker/Lambda/EC2 or GCP AI Platform/Cloud Run - choose one to explore lightly for deployment)
MLflow (experiment tracking, model registry - conceptual and basic hands-on)
resources: Docker Documentation and 'Docker for Developers' tutorials
Cloud provider (AWS/GCP) free tier tutorials for basic deployment

learning_plan.focus: Advanced ML Topics & Data Engineering Essentials

daily_breakdown.1_hour:
Advanced ML Topic Deep Dive (Choose ONE based on interest/market demand, e.g., for NLP/AIE focus): 
    - NLP with Hugging Face Transformers: Text classification, Question Answering, fine-tuning pre-trained models. OR 
    - Advanced Tabular ML: Feature engineering, ensemble methods (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost), model interpretability (SHAP/LIME). OR 
    - Reinforcement Learning Basics: Q-learning, Policy Gradients (if time permits and strong interest).
daily_breakdown.1.5_hours: Project 3: Develop a project using your chosen advanced topic. For example, if NLP: Build a text sentiment analysis web app using Hugging Face Transformers, deployed similarly to Project 2. If Tabular: A robust prediction model on a complex Kaggle tabular dataset, emphasizing feature engineering, model selection, and explainability.

key_topics: NLP (Transformers, word embeddings, tokenization, Hugging Face `transformers` library)
Tabular ML (Gradient Boosting Machines, feature selection, hyperparameter tuning)
Feature Engineering techniques (creating new features from raw data)
Intermediate SQL for data querying and preparation
resources: Kaggle competitions (for tabular data, feature engineering examples, and robust pipelines)
SQLZoo or LeetCode SQL problems for practice

daily_breakdown.1.5_hours: ML System Design: Practice common ML system design questions (e.g., recommendation engine, spam detector, image search, fraud detection, content moderation). Learn a structured approach to breaking down these problems (data, model choice, features, infrastructure, monitoring, scaling, trade-offs).
daily_breakdown.1_hour: Resume/Portfolio/LinkedIn Optimization: Refine all project READMEs on GitHub (clear descriptions, installation, results, live demo links if possible). Create a concise, impactful resume tailored for MLE/AIE roles. Update LinkedIn profile. Practice behavioral questions using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) with examples from your projects and academic experience.

key_topics: ML System Design principles and common patterns
Effective Resume & Portfolio building for tech roles
resources: LeetCode (Premium if possible for company-specific questions)
Grokking the Machine Learning Interview (Educative.io) or similar resources for ML system design
YouTube channels (e.g., System Design Interview) and blogs on ML System Design
ChatGPT/Bard for mock behavioral questions and feedback
LinkedIn for networking and job searching

general_recommendations: **GitHub is Your Portfolio:** Your GitHub profile is crucial. Ensure all projects are live, well-documented with clear READMEs, installation instructions, results, and ideally, a link to a live demo.
**Networking:** Actively connect with other ML engineers and recruiters on LinkedIn. Attend virtual meetups or webinars related to ML/AI.
**Market Research:** Continuously review job descriptions for ML Engineer/AI Engineer roles in your target global markets (e.g., US, Europe, remote jobs) to fine-tune your learning and project focus.
**Consistency is Key:** Stick to the 4-hour daily schedule. Even short, focused sessions are more effective than sporadic long ones. Take short breaks to avoid burnout.
**Prioritize Practical Implementation:** Given the short timeframe, prioritize hands-on building, coding, and deployment over extensive theoretical deep dives into every single topic.
**Mock Interviews:** Practice explaining your projects, technical decisions, and thought processes. Conduct mock coding and system design interviews with peers or mentors if possible.

**English Communication:** For global market jobs, strong English communication skills (both written and verbal) are often as important as technical skills. Practice articulating your thoughts clearly.
